text:
San Jose Hockey Now called Will Smith's three-point night against Nashville the best game of his career, and one of the best in the league this year. At 21, he keeps raising his own ceiling: 8 goals and 19 points in 25 games, 7 of those points on the power play, nearly 20 minutes a night.

If anything he's been unlucky. He has 8 goals on 9.4 expected (the quality of his chances), and his team has scored fewer than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains where the chances come from: 8.3 per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net last season, 98th percentile, and he carries the puck in on 59% of his entries instead of dumping it.

For context, forwards picked second to sixth since 2005 scored a median 0.47 points a game in their first full season. Smith, the fourth pick in 2023, is at 0.76. The open question is defense: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice last season, bottom 8% of forwards. Our season projection sits at 70 points.
headline: Will Smith is ahead of the curve at 21
